en.question: A teammate hardcodes the Anthropic API key in a config file committed to the repository so that CI can run integration tests. What should you do in code review?

options.text: Approve it, provided repository access is limited to the engineering team.
options.note: Access lists change, repositories get forked, and history is permanent.

options.text: Approve it but open a follow-up ticket to move the key later.
options.note: The exposure begins the moment it merges; a ticket does not contain it.

options.text: Reject it, and have CI read the key from an encrypted secret store at run time.
Approve it if the file is added to .gitignore in the same pull request.
options.note: gitignore does not remove a file already tracked and committed.

en.explanation: Committed secrets persist in history, clones, forks, and CI caches. Injecting from a secret store at run time keeps the credential out of the repository entirely.
